walkthroughs.body_html:
Density & Pressure — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Density & Pressure brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Density & Pressure.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 200 g block has volume 100 cm³. Its density is:
options: 0.5 g/cm³
2 g/cm³
20 g/cm³
200 g/cm³

mcqs.q: An object will float in water if:
options: it is light
its mass is less than water's mass
its density is less than water's
it is hollow
Young's modulus measures how strong a material is — how much force it can take before breaking.
Young's modulus measures the density of a material.
The stiffness of a material — the ratio of stress to strain in the elastic region.
It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.

mcqs.q: Does light always travel at the same speed?
options: Only in a vacuum; in any material medium (water, glass) light travels more slowly, which is what causes refraction.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
Yes — c is a universal constant in every situation.
It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.

mcqs.q: What happens to a metal wire stretched beyond its elastic limit?
options: It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.
It snaps immediately at the elastic limit.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
It deforms plastically and will not return to its original length when the load is removed.
